topic: How are link budgets affected when prioritizing high-revenue services versus navigation safety margins in dynamic scheduling?
consensus_response: Dynamic scheduling prioritizes traffic based on QoS parameters, but interference from revenue services can degrade performance metrics like latency and jitter. This occurs due to increased signal strength from high-demand services, leading to reduced capacity.  Channel allocation strategies play a crucial role in optimizing link budgets for both safety-critical navigation and revenue-generating services. Analyzing channel utilization patterns and resource allocation is essential for maintaining balanced network efficiency.
reference_context: Satellite networks prioritize revenue-generating services over navigation safety margins, impacting link budgets through interference and reduced capacity. This tradeoff leads to degraded performance metrics like latency and jitter.  Optimizing link budgets requires analyzing channel utilization patterns and prioritizing resources effectively.
